guitar-chord-finder.assumptionNote: Shapes are movable barre voicings in standard tuning (E A D G B E), shown with sharp note names. Diminished uses an A-shape voicing and the power chord a low three-string voicing. Open-position variants are not shown.
benefits: Get a correct, playable shape for 108 chords - 12 roots times 9 chord types - instantly.
Hear each chord as an arpeggio so you know exactly what it should sound like.
See every chord tone with its interval (R, 3, 5, b7...), which teaches real fretboard theory.
Barre shapes move anywhere on the neck, so one pattern unlocks all twelve keys.

faqs.a: A chord is three or more notes played together. A major chord is root + major third + perfect fifth (1-3-5). A minor chord lowers the third (1-b3-5). Seventh chords add a fourth note a seventh above the root, which is what gives them their jazzy or bluesy colour.
faqs.q: What makes a chord major, minor, or seventh?

faqs.a: In the diagram, vertical lines are the six strings (low E on the left) and horizontal lines are frets. Dots show where to press, the number at the side is the fret position, x means skip the string, and o means play it open. For barre chords, lay your index finger flat across the marked fret.
faqs.q: How do I read the chord diagram?

faqs.a: An E-shape barre has its root on the low E (6th) string - like the F chord at fret 1. An A-shape barre has its root on the A (5th) string - like the B chord at fret 2. Once you learn one shape, sliding it up or down the neck gives you every chord of that type.
faqs.q: What is the difference between an E-shape and an A-shape barre?

faqs.a: Only in spelling, not in sound: C# and Db are the same pitch on guitar. This finder always shows sharps (C#). Classical or jazz charts often prefer flats, but your fingers play the same frets either way.
faqs.q: Is C# the same as Db?

faqs.a: A power chord is just root + fifth (1-5), usually written as a 5 - like G5 or A5. With no third, it is neither major nor minor, which is why it sounds so strong and works over both major and minor riffs in rock and metal.

Yes - tap Play to hear the chord as an arpeggio, one string at a time from low to high. If your version sounds wrong next to it, check the diagram again: the most common mistake is accidentally muting a string that should ring.
faqs.q: Can I hear what the chord sounds like?

guitar-chord-finder.formula:
Major triad: R - 3 - 5 (0, 4, 7 semitones)
Minor triad: R - b3 - 5 (0, 3, 7 semitones)
Dominant 7th: R - 3 - 5 - b7 (0, 4, 7, 10 semitones)
Diminished triad: R - b3 - b5 (0, 3, 6 semitones)
E-shape major at fret f: frets [f, f+2, f+2, f+1, f, f].
howTo: Pick the chord root: any of the 12 notes from C to B.
Choose the chord type: major, minor, 7th, maj7, m7, sus4, sus2, diminished, or power chord.
Read the fretboard diagram: dots are finger positions, x means mute, o means open.
Tap Play to hear the chord as an arpeggio and check your own version against it.
Slide the same shape up or down the neck - the root note on the bass string tells you which chord you are playing.
keyFacts: A major triad stacks a major third and a perfect fifth above the root: C major is C-E-G.
A minor triad lowers the third by one semitone: C minor is C-Eb-G.
Seventh chords add a fourth note: C7 is C-E-G-Bb, Cmaj7 is C-E-G-B.
Barre chords are movable: one E-shape or A-shape pattern plays every chord of its type.
In the diagram, x means do not play the string and o means play it open.
A power chord (5) contains only root and fifth, so it works over both major and minor progressions.

The audio preview is a clean synthesized arpeggio, not a real guitar recording.

guitar-chord-finder.quickAnswer: Pick a root and a chord type to get a correct, playable diagram instantly. For example, C major is an A-shape barre at fret 3: mute the low E, then play frets 3-5-5-5-3 for the notes C-G-C-E-G (root, fifth, root, third, fifth). Every shape here is a movable barre pattern, so sliding it up or down the neck gives you all twelve chords of that type - the root on the bass string names the chord.
guitar-chord-finder.tagline: Pick any root and chord type - get a correct fretboard diagram, notes, intervals, and audio.
guitar-chord-finder.workedExample:
Finding C major:
1. Root = C, type = Major.
2. C sits 3 semitones above the A string, so the finder picks an A-shape barre at fret 3.
3. Frets: low E muted, then 3 - 5 - 5 - 5 - 3.
4. Notes: C3 (root), G3 (fifth), C4 (root), E4 (third), G4 (fifth).
5. Intervals: R - 5 - R - 3 - 5, the major triad formula.
6. Tap Play: you hear C-G-C-E-G arpeggiated from low to high.
